check.asks_recipient.instructions: The text asks the reader to do something.

options.request: The writer asks the reader to do something.
options.promise: The writer commits to doing something.
options.none: The text is neither a request nor a promise.

closure.fulfilled.instructions: The later text shows the obligation has been carried out.

closure.withdrawn.instructions: The later text cancels or withdraws the obligation.

closure.deadline_changed.instructions: The later text sets a different deadline for the obligation.

closure.modified.instructions: The later text changes what the obligation requires.

triage.asks_recipient.instructions: The paragraph asks its recipient to do something.

triage.commits_sender.instructions: The paragraph commits its sender to doing something.

triage.asks_question.instructions: The paragraph asks a genuine question that seeks an answer.

triage.names_time.instructions: The paragraph names a time, date, deadline, or event-relative time.

triage.boilerplate.instructions: The paragraph is a signature, legal footer, unsubscribe notice, or disclaimer.

triage.automated_notification.instructions: The paragraph is an automatically generated notification.

rules.recap.instructions: This email is an automatically generated meeting summary, recap, or transcript.

rules.scoped_event.instructions: This request is about attending, preparing for, or bringing something to a meeting or event.

rules.event_match.instructions: The phrase refers to the named event.

rules.duplicate_action.instructions: These two sentences ask for the same thing.

rules.thread_merge.instructions: These two messages belong to the same conversation topic.

rules.deadline_kind.instructions: Classify how the phrase expresses a deadline.

options.event_tied: The deadline is tied to a named event.
options.soft: The timing is flexible or aspirational.
options.unknown: The phrase has no supported deadline classification.
